one_liner: Windows kernel-mode UTF-8/UTF-16 substring search (last-character SIMD scan plus BMH/SWAR fallback) beating kernel CRT strstr/wcsstr on buffers above 6 KB.
what_it_does: Two classes, CKmStrSearch8 (char) and CKmStrSearch16 (wchar_t), for use inside Windows kernel drivers: Initialize(pattern, len) builds a Boyer-Moore-Horspool skip table in paged pool, then Find(text, len, engine) returns the zero-based index of the first match or -1. Text is length-bounded, so buffers need no NUL terminator and may contain embedded NULs. Callers can force Scalar, AVX2, AVX512 or NEON, or let 'Auto' route by buffer size.
how_it_is_fast: For patterns under 128 (AVX2/NEON) or 256 (AVX-512) characters, the vector engines broadcast the pattern's last character and compare 128 or 256 bytes per iteration (4x unrolled cmpeq, OR-reduced, then bit-scan), checking the first character and the middle only at candidate positions; longer patterns add a BMH jump after each 64- or 128-character block. Below 6 KB (1 KB on ARM64) Auto stays in general-purpose registers (scalar BMH with a SWAR memchr fast-forward when the skip is 2 or less) to avoid the KeSaveExtendedProcessorState/XSAVE cost of using YMM/ZMM in ring 0, and AVX-512 is used only from 20 KB. The UTF-16 skip table is folded to 2,048 entries (8 KB) with a golden-ratio multiplicative hash, keeping the smallest shift on collisions.
when_to_use: Inside a Windows kernel driver at PASSIVE_LEVEL or APC_LEVEL, searching buffers larger than about 6 KB (8-bit) for a fixed pattern that is set up once and reused.
Length-delimited kernel buffers (UNICODE_STRING-style, not NUL-terminated, possibly with embedded NULs), which strstr/wcsstr cannot take directly.
Repetitive text where kernel CRT strstr goes quadratic on partial matches of the pattern's first character ('aaaaaaaaab' in all-'a' text: 0.21 GB/s CRT versus 81.67 GB/s Smart Auto on the i7-1165G7).
AVX-512BW hosts scanning buffers of 20 KB or more, where the README shows the ZMM path ahead of AVX2 (1 MB: 80.92 vs 65.46 GB/s for 8-bit).
when_not_to_use: Buffers under about 6 KB on bare metal: Auto runs the scalar path, which measured 2-3x slower than CRT strstr (8-bit 256 B: 4.88 vs 15.03 GB/s; 40 B: 1.95 vs 3.61 GB/s).

Text in which the pattern's last character is common: every occurrence becomes a candidate with a first-character check and a forward middle verification, so a pattern like 'aaaaaaaaba' over runs of 'a' does O(N*M) work in the vector path (inferred from FindAVX2/FindAVX512, not measured by the repo).
DISPATCH_LEVEL or higher: Find is PAGED_CODE and reads a paged-pool skip table, despite a header comment about calling it at DISPATCH_LEVEL.
User-mode code: the classes include ntddk.h and use kernel pool and XSTATE APIs, and the README says TestUm timings cannot be trusted; use a user-mode searcher instead.
Production code that needs maturity: 4 commits, 0 stars, single author, no CI, and texts longer than INT_MAX characters are not rejected although Find returns int.

integration.dependencies: Windows Driver Kit (ntddk.h, ExAllocatePool2, KeSaveExtendedProcessorState/KeSaveFloatingPointState, ExIsProcessorFeaturePresent); intrin.h/immintrin.h or arm64_neon.h
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (/std:c++20, [[likely]]/[[unlikely]]), MSVC with the WindowsKernelModeDriver10.0 toolset; README names Visual Studio 2026 and the latest WDK
integration.platforms: Windows kernel on x64 (SWAR, AVX2, AVX-512F+BW detected via CPUID) and ARM64 (NEON); the project has only x64 and ARM64 configurations
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Find is a const method that only reads the pattern and the skip table, so concurrent Find calls on one initialized object look safe by inspection; Initialize is not re-entrant and a second call leaks the first table
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces strstr/wcsstr only after rewriting the call: a two-step object API (Initialize then Find) that takes an explicit text length and returns an int index rather than a pointer, and the pattern buffer must outlive the object (shallow copy)

gotchas: All three throughput inputs are memchr-degenerate for the hybrid: the last pattern character ('k' of 'Needle In The Haystack', 'b' of 'aaaaaaaaab', 'K' of 'CRITICAL: USE_AFTER_FREE BUGCHECK') never occurs in the text except at the planted match, and every pattern is below the 128/256-character bifurcation, so the vector engines never verify a candidate or use the skip table; the 45-105 GB/s figures are single-byte vector scans. The 'realistic log corpus' line contains no 'K' and no uppercase 'C', so it exercises neither skip-table entropy nor CRT candidate checks.

Harness accounting: every second call searches from offset 32 with length minus 32 but is credited with the full buffer; at 40 B that leaves 8 characters, shorter than the 22- or 33-character pattern, so Find returns -1 without searching, which inflates every engine's tiny-buffer GB/s (about 6% at 256 B). Each cell is one 2 s single-thread run (the README's 'multi-threaded' claim does not match StartThreads(pMgr, 1, ...)); identical code paths differ by up to 40% in the VMware tables (8-bit 10 KB Smart Auto 18.61 vs AVX2 Explicit 31.17 GB/s, both FindAVX2) and by about 6% on bare metal (1 MB 85.93 vs 80.92, both FindAVX512).

The correctness suite never reaches the 8-bit AVX2/AVX-512 loops or the 16-bit AVX-512 loop: its texts are 104 characters or fewer, below the 128/256-character minimums, so those engines fall back to FindScalar; the long-pattern BMH-plus-vector branch is untested, and the throughput loop does not check returned indices. Reading the loops found no off-by-one, but there is no test evidence for them.

The header says a forced AVX512 engine falls back to scalar below 20 KB, but the code only falls back below 256 characters, so explicit AVX512 pays the ZMM state save on small buffers; with 16-bit text exactly at the 20 KB threshold the harness's 32-character shift makes Auto alternate between AVX-512 and AVX2 on successive calls.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued substring searchers (MSVC STL's vectorized std::search, sliceslice, strstr.c, AOCL-LibMem) are user-mode; pick KmStrSearch only inside a Windows kernel driver scanning buffers above about 6 KB, and use MSVC STL std::search or a user-mode library everywhere else.
verified_claims_summary: A single-thread kernel-driver loop (2 s per cell, Windows 11, MSVC version and Release/Debug unstated) measured 8-bit Smart Auto at 45.71 GB/s versus kernel CRT strstr 22.38 GB/s at 10 KB and 85.93 vs 22.66 GB/s at 1 MB on a bare-metal i7-1165G7 (about 2.0x and 3.8x, derived from page data), with a pattern whose last character never appears in the text; on that input and the log input CRT wins at 40 B and 256 B. The 'up to 385x' figure is 'aaaaaaaaab' over all-'a' text, where CRT strstr falls to 0.21 GB/s while the hybrid runs a vector scan for 'b'.
status_note: Active (four commits from 2026-08-25 to 2026-09-07, 0 stars) and MIT-licensed; a small two-class source drop for Windows kernel drivers, best treated as research code that needs your own large-buffer correctness tests before production use.
